name: Tessera Industries Optical Fiber Tap Detector OFT-1
product_name: Tessera Industries Optical Fiber Tap Detector OFT-1
description: A diagnostic tool that detects unauthorized taps on fiber-optic cables by measuring signal loss at micro-dB resolution — far more sensitive than standard network monitoring equipment. The OFT-1 sends a calibrated light pulse through a fiber and measures the return signal with precision that can identify the 0.1 dB loss caused by a micro-bend optical tap. The device maps the location of any detected tap to within 10 cm along the fiber run, allowing physical identification and removal. Tessera developed it as a counter to their own OT-1 optical tap — and sells both the attack and the defense.

specifications.output: Fiber loss map with anomaly flags

story_hooks: An OFT-1 sweep of a corporate network found 23 unauthorized optical taps across the facility — some had been in place for over two years, and the combined data loss is measured in petabytes.

A Tessera OFT-1 has been found to have a firmware modification that causes it to report clean results on fibers that actually have taps — the counter-surveillance tool has been sabotaged to protect existing surveillance.
